name: South Carolina
tagline: From the Blue Ridge foothills to the Sea Islands, by way of oak-shaded plantation roads and Lowcountry marsh.
intro: South Carolina's byways run along the foot of the Blue Ridge and down the Savannah River lakes, cross the York County farm country and the old rice lands of the Pee Dee, and wander the oak-lined roads and marsh causeways around Charleston and Beaufort. This chapter follows the South Carolina Scenic Byways program, which SCDOT runs with the South Carolina Scenic Highways Committee; unusually, each road is designated by an act of the General Assembly, so the statute gives every route's exact streets, and many acts also ban billboards or protect roadside trees. The Forest Service's Oscar Wigington byway, which shares road with the state's Falling Waters route, is listed separately.

members.name: Ashley River Road National Scenic Byway
members.blurb: SC 61 follows the Ashley River for eleven miles north of Church Creek under oak canopy, passing St. Andrew's Church, Drayton Hall and Middleton Place, three national historic landmarks within one historic district.

members.name: Cherokee Foothills National Scenic Byway
members.blurb: SC 11 swings 112 miles between I-85 at Gaffney and I-85 at the Georgia line, through peach orchards and foothill villages under Table Rock and Caesars Head, crossing Lake Keowee and passing Cowpens battlefield.

members.name: Edisto Island National Scenic Byway
members.blurb: SC 174 crosses the McKinley Washington Jr. Bridge at Dawhoo Creek and runs the length of Edisto Island through salt marsh and maritime forest, past farm stands selling sweetgrass baskets, to the beach at Edisto Beach State Park.

members.name: Savannah River National Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Five state highways run a hundred miles down the Savannah River side of the state, from Oakway through Starr and McCormick, with its old railroad depot, to the Georgia line below Clarks Hill, skirting Hartwell, Russell and Thurmond lakes.

members.name: Bohicket Road Scenic Highway
members.blurb: Ten miles of Bohicket Road cross Johns Island toward Kiawah and Seabrook, busy with island traffic now but still a handsome road, near the Angel Oak, a live oak thought to be more than four centuries old.

members.name: Cowpens National Battlefield Scenic Byway
members.blurb: SC 110 runs nine miles north from the town of Cowpens through farm country to the Cherokee Foothills highway at SC 11, the easy way in from I-85 to Cowpens National Battlefield.

members.name: Edisto Beach Scenic Highway
members.blurb: SC 174 runs its last three miles through the town of Edisto Beach, along the beachfront on Palmetto Boulevard and down to the marina on Big Bay Creek.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Falling Waters Scenic Byway
members.blurb: SC 107 climbs north from Walhalla through Sumter National Forest to the North Carolina line, with a fork across to SC 130, passing Issaqueena Falls, the Stumphouse Mountain Tunnel and the Wigington overlook above Lake Jocassee.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Fort Johnson Road Scenic Highway
members.blurb: Fort Johnson Road runs four and a half miles across James Island, from Folly Road out to the state Department of Natural Resources' Marine Resources Center at the end of the road.

members.name: Hilton Head Scenic Highway
members.blurb: Despite its name, this one stays inland, eight miles of four-lane US 278 from I-95 near Hardeeville to the Beaufort County line, mostly undeveloped and free of billboards, busy with traffic bound for Bluffton and the islands.

members.name: Hilton Head Island Scenic Byway
members.blurb: US 278 runs 22 miles from SC 170 out to Hilton Head Island and ends at Sea Pines Circle, a busy multi-lane road kept tidy by landscaped medians and local rules on setbacks and signs.
members.note: Shown on the map as US-278 Scenic Highway.

members.name: Long Point Road Scenic Highway
members.blurb: Two miles of Long Point Road in Mount Pleasant pass Boone Hall Plantation and the Charles Pinckney National Historic Site, and state law keeps the larger roadside trees from being cut without permission.

members.name: Mathis Ferry Road Scenic Highway
members.blurb: Mathis Ferry Road has been a scenic highway since 1988, under three miles through Mount Pleasant from Whipple Road to 7th Street. Houses have filled in along it, but the trees and two historical markers remain.

members.name: May River Scenic Byway
members.blurb: SC 46 runs from the Jasper County line into old Bluffton under oak canopy and past wetlands, then turns down Boundary and Bridge streets onto Alljoy Road, ending at Brighton Beach on the May River.
members.note: Shown on the map as SC-46 Scenic Highway.

members.name: McTeer Bridge & Causeways Scenic Highway
members.blurb: Under three miles between Port Royal and Lady's Island, most of the view from the McTeer Bridge itself, over the Beaufort River with marsh and a marina below and the Beaufort waterfront to the north.
members.note: Shown on the map as James Edwin McTeer Bridge & The Causways Scenic Highway.

members.name: Old Sheldon Church Road Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Old Sheldon Church Road runs about seven miles between Gardens Corner and Yemassee under oak canopy and past plantations, with the ruins of Sheldon Church, dating to the 1740s, beside the road.

members.name: Plantersville Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Choppee and Plantersville roads make a twelve-mile loop off US 701 beside the Great Pee Dee River, through old rice-growing country thick with historic sites, past the state's Samworth Plantation wildlife area.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Riverland Drive Scenic Highway
members.blurb: Riverland Drive runs five miles across James Island, less than three miles from downtown Charleston, along tree-lined streets and an undeveloped stretch under oak canopy, past wetlands and two public parks.

members.name: SC 170 Scenic Highway
members.blurb: Eight miles of four-lane SC 170 run from Okatie east to the Broad River Bridge with little roadside business and long open views, on the main road between Beaufort and the Bluffton side of the county.

members.name: US 21 Scenic Highway
members.blurb: US 21 runs about nineteen miles out across the Sea Islands from Beaufort, a road of wide marsh views sometimes called the Sea Island Scenic Highway, ending at Hunting Island State Park and its lighthouse.

members.name: Western York County Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Some sixty miles of state highways run from Kings Mountain National Military Park south through York to Historic Brattonsville, then circle north through McConnells, Sharon and Hickory Grove to tiny Smyrna, among hayfields and old cotton gins.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Piedmont Gateway Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Designated in 2024, this 26-mile route follows US 21 north from Ridgeway, then Mobley Highway west across I-77 to White Oak, passing National Register sites in both towns and a historic African American church camp.
members.note: No route line: the national dataset does not include this road and the state publishes no map line for it.

members.name: Oscar Wigington Scenic Byway
members.blurb: SC 107 climbs north from the Cherokee Foothills highway through Sumter National Forest, past Moody Spring and Cherry Hill campground, with a turn onto SC 413 for the Wigington Overlook above Lake Jocassee.
